answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-slash identity bond: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit that is forfeited if peers prove it ran duplicate identities. Like dawn breaking over a market, the bond makes each new identity costly, so an attacker who spawns a thousand clones pays a thousand times. An onyx ledger records every bond and slash immutably, while an ivory-list of verified agents lets honest participants trade faster without re-checking every newcomer. The cost scales with the attack, not with honest use.
